chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Adhan and the Iqamah are thirty-five letters,' and he counted them with his hand, one by one: the Adhan is eighteen letters, and the Iqamah is seventeen letters.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir, the sixth Imam
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: The call to establish the prayer

ai.seo_question: How many words are in the Adhan and Iqamah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) enumerates the specific letter count of the Adhan and Iqamah, providing a precise metric for the liturgical structure of the call to prayer. This narration highlights the meticulous attention to detail in Shia jurisprudence regarding the recitation of these calls, distinguishing the Adhan (eighteen letters) from the Iqamah (seventeen letters) as transmitted through the chain of Aban ibn Uthman and Isma'il al-Ju'fi. It underscores the sacred nature of the verbal formulae that precede the communal prayer.
